$comment: P4.D175 — the shared corpus for v4's REAL `clear-generated-image-placeholder-descriptions-v1` migration (v4 `78b381a96`, bug 132) and v5's `db::generated_image_placeholder_heal`. `files` rows are the MAIN partition; `links` are `doc_mount_file_links` in the MOUNT partition. The dash in the wardrobe label is U+2014 with a space either side, exactly as the writer rendered it — a hyphen there matches NOTHING and would make every wardrobe arm vacuous.

scenarios.name: both-labels-cleared
scenarios.$comment: The two shapes the writers produced, on GENERATED files and on image links. Every one clears; the sentence is the plural form.

scenarios.name: uploaded-file-survives
scenarios.$comment: `source = 'GENERATED'` is a conjunct on the FILES side only. A row an operator uploaded that happens to carry a matching caption is NOT touched — and its updatedAt must not move either.

Story background for: A Quiet Afternoon

scenarios.name: non-image-link-survives
scenarios.$comment: The link side has no source column, so it gates on the MIME type instead. A markdown document whose description happens to match is left alone.

links.description: Story background for: The Long Road
Story background for: The Long Road

scenarios.name: outfit-preview-survives-the-narrow-predicate
scenarios.$comment: ⚠ THE CONVERGENCE TRIPWIRE. A THIRD v4 writer (app/api/v1/wardrobe/preview-avatar/route.ts:160,:185) stamps `<Name> — outfit preview` with source='GENERATED', and v4's own fix does not touch it — `78b381a96` does not open that file, and the predicate does not match the label. v5 reproduces that EXACTLY (api/wardrobe.rs:1112) and files it upstream instead of widening the predicate. This row must SURVIVE on both sides; it goes red by design the day v4 widens.

scenarios.name: near-misses-survive
scenarios.$comment: The predicate is anchored: 'Story background for: %' must be a PREFIX, '% — wardrobe portrait' a SUFFIX. A row that merely mentions either phrase mid-string is untouched, and so is a wardrobe label written with a plain hyphen.

files.description: A note about the Story background for: X

scenarios.name: singular-sentence
scenarios.$comment: Exactly one of each: the message's two singular forms, which a plural-only corpus would never render.

scenarios.name: links-only-files-clean
scenarios.$comment: The files side has nothing; the link side does. v4's shouldRun() only inspects the mount when the files count is ZERO, so this is the arm that exercises that second probe.

files.description: a real description of a real picture

scenarios.name: no-mount-index-skips-the-links
scenarios.$comment: No mount partition at all. The files side still clears; linksSkipped is true and the sentence gains its parenthetical. NOTE this arm is silent — v4 warns only from its catch, never from the plain else.

scenarios.name: links-table-missing-a-column
scenarios.$comment: The mount partition is there but its links table predates `originalMimeType`, so `linksTableUsable` is false — the same skipped arm reached a different way.

scenarios.name: nothing-matches-anywhere
scenarios.$comment: v4's shouldRun() is FALSE, so its runner skips and records NOTHING; v5 returns NotApplicable and records nothing. Unlike the sha256 realign, the two ledgers agree here — this migration's shouldRun tests DRIFT, not presence.

scenarios.name: ledger-row-present-leaves-everything
scenarios.$comment: A migrations_state row is already there — v4 having run its own migration on the shared instance (the cross-app leg, in the direction that actually happens). Both sides refuse at the completed check, and the labels below are STILL THERE afterwards, so a heal that ignored the ledger would clear them and this arm would redden.
